Q136.headline: 519 of 525 questions mappable to targets; hybrid recall unmeasured — engrim's semantic model is not available in the room. Recorded as blocked with its reason; follow-up is to pre-cache the model or rerun lexical-only as a stated partial.

Q137.headline: PASS — provenance intact on all 4 fixture records; contradictions retained, both versions retrieved, nothing silently resolved.

Q281.headline: Early signal barely predicts outcomes out of sample: held-out AUC 0.690 vs train 0.863; OLS R2 0.012. Logs carry status and cost but NO quality labels — this predicts log status, not quality.

Q364.headline: The routed advantage survives repricing at Hydra's own mix (65–72% cheaper, ratio 1.0) — but under asymmetric caching (global history cached 80% vs routed 40%) savings shrink to 9.6–27.7%. Router break-even: a router call may cost up to 65–72% of the global-history cost before routing loses.

Q401.headline: The paper's own formula at its own stated values gives 33.3x, not the printed 26x. Exactly 26x needs rho_u = 0.0285 (at r = 0.01) or r = 0.0185 (at rho_u = 0.02) — an unexplained extra cost fraction of 0.0085.

Q471.headline: Verdict: weakens — e-means at 2.5 epochs matched or beat Lloyd-25 loss in 0 of 6 text cells (per-cell median loss ratio 1.0022–1.0092, i.e. 0.22–0.92% worse); 28 of 60 text runs reached target within 2.5 epochs, median 3.0 epochs to target where reached, and synthetic ARI was 0.950 for e-means at 2.5 epochs vs 0.953 for Lloyd-25. Scope: n ≤ 648 TF-IDF/SVD text embeddings with a heuristic batch/decay schedule (the authors' scaling-law formulas are not printed in the card); this bears on the small-n, off-family question only, not on the card's large-scale GPU claims.

Q472.headline: e-means' cost advantage widens with n on synthetic mixtures: wall-time scaling exponents Lloyd 1.103 (easy separable) / 1.088 (hard overlapping) vs e-means 0.723 / 0.730 — gaps of +0.379 and +0.357, both beyond 2SE — and distance-evaluation exponents point the same way. e-means reached Lloyd-25's target within 5 epochs in 119 of 120 cells (94 within 2.5 epochs; median 1.5 epochs to target where reached) and beat Lloyd-25 loss at 2.5 epochs in 51 cells, but the loss flip is cell-dependent (hard overlapping: 0/4 k values at n=500 and n=2000, 4/4 at n=128000), while the time-to-target advantage grows with n.

Q505.headline: YES — capping retries at budget tier 1 halves the p90 quota cost (46 → 23, -50%) on multi-attempt job families, and the ok-outcome rate is flat (0.196 at every tier): extra retries spend quota without buying more successes.
